resources.string: Before you send money, check with your child that the request really came from them.
Family Shield never tells you to send money. Only your child\'s own answer turns a check green or red.

Pilot notice: Family Shield, Cartesia (voice-note transcription), Twilio (calls and text codes), Anthropic (reading the message for patterns), and Google (sign-in and notifications) process what a check needs. We do not build a voiceprint.
This build has no way to sign in. It needs a Google server client id.
No Google account is available on this device. Add one in Settings, then try again.
Google sign-in didn\'t finish. Please try again.
You\'ll add your children next. Each child joins with a one-time invite code, or by a text link if they won\'t install the app.
A parent sent you a one-time code. You\'ll join as their child.
Your family membership isn\'t active yet
Ask the parent who created the family to check the Family Shield app.
Add a child to start. They join with a one-time invite code, or by a text link if they won\'t install the app.
Can\'t verify yet: %1$s hasn\'t joined. Their invite code works until %2$s.
Can\'t verify yet: %1$s hasn\'t joined, and the invite code expired.
Can\'t verify yet: %1$s joined but hasn\'t verified a phone number.
Can\'t verify yet: we texted a link to the number ending %2$s. %1$s needs to tap Allow and choose a check code.
Can\'t verify yet: %1$s isn\'t set up.
Confirm only if you recognize this number. If you don\'t, reject it.
%1$s wants to change their number to one ending %2$s.
Calls go to the new number only after you confirm. Confirming ends any check for %1$s that is still open.
%1$s\'s number now ends %2$s. Checks that were still open for %1$s were stopped.
We texted a link to the number ending %2$s. %1$s needs to tap Allow and choose a 4-digit check code.
They\'ll use the Family Shield app
You\'ll get a one-time invite code to send them.
We text them a link. They tap Allow and choose a 4-digit check code; you never see it. Only +1 (US, Canada) and +82 (Korea) numbers.
Their mobile number, with country code
Send this code to %1$s over a chat you already trust, like a KakaoTalk or iMessage thread you\'ve used before. It works once, for 24 hours. We show it only now.
Your Family Shield invite code: %1$s\nInstall Family Shield, sign in, and enter this code. It works once, within 24 hours.
Who does the message say it\'s from?
No child can be verified yet. A child needs to join, verify their number, and be confirmed by you first.
Paste the message you got, if you like. It is used only to point out known scam patterns, and it is deleted 30 days after the check.
We ask your child in the Family Shield app first, then call the number they verified. Only their answer decides the result. Don\'t send money while we check.
Nothing is sent until you tap Verify.
Voice note attached: %1$s (%2$d KB). It stays on this phone until you tap Verify.
That voice note is over 10 MB, so it wasn\'t attached. You can paste the message instead.
That voice note was empty, so it wasn\'t attached.
Family Shield can\'t read that file as a voice note. You can paste the message instead.
That voice note couldn\'t be read. You can paste the message instead.
A message is waiting. Sign in as a parent. Nothing is sent until you tap Verify.
A message is waiting. Create your family, then choose who to ask. Nothing is sent until you tap Verify.
This account is a child, so it can\'t verify a message. Sign in as a parent. Nothing was sent.
We asked %1$s to confirm in the Family Shield app. If there\'s no answer in 90 seconds, we\'ll call the number they verified.
We\'re calling %1$s on the number they verified. They enter a code on the keypad, then tell us whether they sent the message.
%1$s entered the right code. Waiting for their answer.
Can\'t update right now. We\'ll keep trying.
What the voice note claims (this does NOT prove who it is)
%1$s confirmed they sent it. The request really came from %1$s. Talk to %1$s directly before sending anything.
%1$s confirmed they did not send this. Do not send money and do not reply to whoever contacted you.
There is no verified number for %1$s, so no call was made. Don\'t send money. Call your child on the number you already know.
We couldn\'t reach %1$s. Don\'t send money. Try calling them on the number you already know.
%1$s hasn\'t entered the check code yet. They may just be busy. Don\'t send money until you reach them yourself.
The check code entered at %2$s was wrong. Don\'t send money. Call your child on the number you already know.
%1$s entered the check code but didn\'t say whether they sent that message. Don\'t send money until you talk to %1$s directly.
We couldn\'t reach %1$s: the Family Shield app on their phone can\'t get our request, and there is no verified number to call. Don\'t send money. Call your child on the number you already know.
We couldn\'t check %1$s\'s code. Don\'t send money. They can set a new check code in the app.

%1$s said yes on a call to a number that was registered or changed in the last 24 hours. That is not confirmed. Don\'t send money. Talk to %1$s on the number you already knew, or wait and check again from the app.
We couldn\'t confirm it was %1$s. Don\'t send money. Call them on a number you already know.
This message looked like a known pattern (%1$s), but %2$s confirmed they sent it. Avoid gift cards, crypto, and wire transfers; they are hard to reverse.
This message looks like a known scam pattern: %1$s. That alone decides nothing; only %2$s\'s own answer does.
a fake arrest and bail demand
a request to keep it secret
Scammers who copy one person\'s voice often try other relatives next. Copy this into your family group chat:

⚠️ Family alert: someone is pretending to be %1$s, possibly with an AI copy of their voice, to ask for money. %1$s confirmed it wasn\'t them. If you get a call, voice note or text from \"%1$s\" asking for money, don\'t pay. Hang up and call %1$s on their saved number. Never pay by gift cards, crypto or wire transfer.

⚠️ Family alert: someone is pretending to be %1$s, possibly with an AI copy of their voice, to ask for money. %1$s confirmed it wasn\'t them. The story used: \"%2$s\". If you get a call, voice note or text from \"%1$s\" asking for money, don\'t pay. Hang up and call %1$s on their saved number. Never pay by gift cards, crypto or wire transfer.

Enter the invite code your parent sent. This account is for you, not for a younger sibling.
Family Shield texts a 6-digit code to prove this number is yours. Only +1 (US, Canada) and +82 (Korea). Your parent never sees your check code.
This account already has a phone number.
We sent a 6-digit code to the number ending %1$s. It expires in 10 minutes.
We sent a 6-digit code to your phone. It expires in 10 minutes.
Call me with the code instead
Pick 4 digits you\'ll remember and enter them twice. Your parent never sees them. If you forget them, you can set new ones after a fingerprint or face check.
Those don\'t match. Enter the same 4 digits twice.
Ask your parent to confirm you in Family Shield. Until they do, they can\'t start a check.
Ask your parent to confirm you in Family Shield. Your number ends in %1$s.

No request right now. When your family asks Family Shield to check a message, you\'ll get a notification. The notification has no Yes or No button and no code. Open it, then confirm with your fingerprint or face to answer.
Your family is waiting for your answer.
Did you send your family a message asking for money?
Only your answer changes the result. Not now leaves the check open, and your family may call you.
Show the code for this call
Your family is calling. The 6-digit code stays hidden until you confirm with your fingerprint or face. It is not in the notification.
Enter this code on the phone keypad, then press 1 for yes or 2 for no. It works once, for 5 minutes, and it is not saved on this phone.
This call wants your 4-digit check code. If it asked for 6 digits, press star, then enter your check code.
Confirm with your fingerprint or face first. Then enter a new 4-digit code twice. This replaces the old one.
This account already has a check code. Replacing it needs a fingerprint or face check.
This check ended without your answer.
Family Shield needs you to confirm a request.
Family Shield uses a strong biometric. The device passcode is only there when a biometric isn\'t available.
That invite code isn\'t valid. Ask your parent for a new one.

Optional. The check code works without this. This labels one number, the number Family Shield calls from, as Family Shield, so the phone does not treat that call as an unknown caller. It does not mark your number or any other number as genuine. On Android, only one app can hold call screening, so turning this on replaces another screening app.
This phone doesn\'t offer call screening. The check code still works.
